records.title: Grain-boundary resistance in Li6PS5Br
records.abstract: This report isolates grain-boundary versus bulk contributions to total resistance using variable-temperature impedance analysis for Li6PS5Br, a member of the sulfide argyrodite family. Samples were prepared via standard solid-state or wet-chemical routes appropriate to this material class and characterized using complementary structural and electrochemical techniques. The results show a trade-off in which gains in one property come at the cost of another, consistent with prior trends in related systems. These findings are discussed in the context of designing next-generation solid electrolytes for lithium-metal batteries, with attention to how grain-boundary resistance relates to overall cell performance and manufacturability.

protocol_steps: Synthesize target composition via solid-state reaction or co-precipitation, per the proposed dopant stoichiometry.
Sinter pressed pellets under controlled atmosphere; vary sintering temperature/time as the primary process variable.
Characterize phase purity via XRD and microstructure via SEM.
Measure ionic conductivity via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) across a temperature series to extract activation energy.
Assemble symmetric Li|electrolyte|Li cells; measure critical current density via stepped current cycling.
experiment_design.toy_simulation_code:
import math
# Toy Arrhenius model: sigma(T) = sigma0 * exp(-Ea / (k_B * T))
k_B = 8.617333262e-5  # eV/K
sigma0 = 1.0e4  # S/cm, prefactor (order-of-magnitude placeholder)
Ea_baseline = 0.35  # eV, undoped baseline
Ea_doped = 0.28  # eV, hypothesized reduction from doping
T = 298.15  # K, room temperature
sigma_baseline = sigma0 * math.exp(-Ea_baseline / (k_B * T))
sigma_doped = sigma0 * math.exp(-Ea_doped / (k_B * T))
improvement_factor = sigma_doped / sigma_baseline
print(f'baseline_conductivity_S_cm={sigma_baseline:.6e}')
print(f'doped_conductivity_S_cm={sigma_doped:.6e}')
print(f'improvement_factor={improvement_factor:.3f}')

import math
# Toy Arrhenius model: sigma(T) = sigma0 * exp(-Ea / (k_B * T))
k_B = 8.617333262e-5  # eV/K
sigma0 = 1.0e4  # S/cm, prefactor (order-of-magnitude placeholder)
Ea_baseline = 0.35  # eV, undoped baseline
Ea_doped = 0.28  # eV, hypothesized reduction from doping
T = 298.15  # K, room temperature
sigma_baseline = sigma0 * math.exp(-Ea_baseline / (k_B * T))
sigma_doped = sigma0 * math.exp(-Ea_doped / (k_B * T))
improvement_factor = sigma_doped / sigma_baseline
print(f'baseline_conductivity_S_cm={sigma_baseline:.6e}')
print(f'doped_conductivity_S_cm={sigma_doped:.6e}')
print(f'improvement_factor={improvement_factor:.3f}')
